{
  "id": "SPEC-ARCH-003",
  "spec_file_path": ".claude/specs/napi-rendering-boundary-newtypes.json",
  "purpose": "Eliminate the defect class 'unvalidated, per-call-site numeric coercion at the NAPI boundary' for the rendering-domain inputs of the michi facade crate. SPEC-ARCH-002 attempted to close this class across the whole of src/napi.rs in one cycle and was rejected by an adversarial gate as oversized: 16 acceptance criteria, 8 newtypes, ~14 call sites, and two unrelated consumer domains (rendering and resilience) whose behavior changes have different blast radii and different reviewers. SPEC-ARCH-003 is the rendering-domain half of that split; a sibling spec will cover the resilience half. The class being eliminated is this: every JavaScript number that crosses into a michi-toon / michi-core rendering call today picks its own Rust width and its own out-of-domain policy, independently, at the call site. As of the current source that is four mutually incompatible policies over five inputs -- src/napi.rs:136 turns a negative JsToonOptions.total_count into None (field silently omitted), src/napi.rs:258 turns a negative render_kv total_count into Some(0) (field silently reported as zero), src/napi.rs:518 turns a negative JsAgentResponse::total_count into 0, src/napi.rs:220 turns a negative truncate max_chars into 0, src/napi.rs:237 clamps decimals_val into [0,20], and src/napi.rs:56/87/238 accepts a raw f64 float_val with no finiteness check at all so a JS NaN reaches michi_toon::Value::Float and is emitted as a quoted "NaN" token. Because napi-rs maps an i32 field onto napi_get_value_int32, which performs ToInt32 wraparound and still returns napi_ok, the value is already mutated before any michi code runs and the call-site policy then normalizes the corrupted value in whichever direction that site happened to choose. This spec deletes the narrowing step from the set of expressible programs: the boundary declares validating newtypes that already store the target Rust type, so there is no coercion left at a call site for a future developer to invent a fifth policy for.",
  "scope": "The inbound JavaScript-number positions of src/napi.rs that feed michi-toon and michi-core rendering, and the new shared kernel module that owns their conversion.

NEW MODULE: src/napi/num.rs, declared as `pub mod num;` inside src/napi.rs (Rust 2018 permits src/napi.rs to coexist with submodules under src/napi/, so src/napi.rs is not moved to mod.rs). The declaration MUST be `pub mod num;`, not a bare `mod num;`: AC-005 requires the integration test tests/napi_num_reuse.rs -- a file outside the crate's own module tree -- to name `michi::napi::num::JsRanged`, which is a hard E0603 (module is private) if the module is not public. Because src/lib.rs carries `#![warn(missing_docs)]`, the `pub mod num;` declaration requires a `///` doc comment, as does every `pub` item defined inside it. This file is the SHARED KERNEL for the whole NAPI numeric boundary, not a rendering-only module: it defines the generic `JsRanged<const MIN: i64, const MAX: i64>` here, in this spec, because this is the first of the two domain specs to land. A later resilience-domain spec will add its own type aliases (for HTTP status codes, retry counts, and delay floats) to this same file, reusing JsRanged and JsFloat without redefining them. Nothing in this spec's implementation may make JsRanged private to the rendering aliases or specialize it to [0,20].

CONVERSION MECHANISM (shared by every newtype in src/napi/num.rs): each newtype implements `napi::bindgen_prelude::FromNapiValue` by reading the incoming JS value as an f64 through `f64::from_napi_value` (which lowers to `napi_get_value_double`, a non-coercing read that errors on a non-number), then routing that f64 through the newtype's `TryFrom<f64>` impl. No newtype ever reads the value as an i32 or u32, so `napi_get_value_int32`'s ToInt32 wraparound is never in the path and the raw JS value reaches validation unmutated. A `TryFrom<f64>` failure becomes `napi::Error::new(napi::Status::InvalidArg, <message>)`, which napi-derive-generated glue throws to JS before the wrapped function body runs. Because `#[napi(object)]` generates both directions for a struct, each newtype also implements `ToNapiValue`, writing the stored value back as a JS double. FromNapiValue/ToNapiValue bodies are `unsafe fn` per the napi-rs trait signatures; this is permitted here (not hand-written unsafe requiring separate justification) because src/napi.rs:21's crate-level `#![allow(unsafe_code)]` already scopes the entire napi module -- including src/napi/num.rs as its child -- as the project's designated FFI boundary exemption per CLAUDE.md's 'No unsafe outside napi boundary' non-negotiable.

ADDITIONAL REQUIRED TRAIT IMPLS AND TYPESCRIPT OVERRIDES (verified against napi-derive-backend 5.1.1, the version actually resolved by this workspace's Cargo.lock for napi-derive = "3"): FromNapiValue and ToNapiValue alone are NOT sufficient. (a) napi-derive's codegen for every `#[napi]` function argument emits a call to `ValidateNapiValue`, so each newtype must additionally implement `napi::bindgen_prelude::TypeName` -- with `type_name()` returning the newtype's own name and `value_type()` returning `napi::ValueType::Number` -- and `napi::bindgen_prelude::ValidateNapiValue` (an empty impl body suffices; its default `validate` delegates to `TypeName::value_type`). Without both, every converted `#[napi]` function fails to compile with an unsatisfied trait bound. (b) napi-rs's TypeScript generator falls through to emitting the Rust type name VERBATIM for any type absent from its hardcoded known-types table, so an unannotated `max_chars: JsCount` would surface in packages/michi-node/index.d.ts as `maxChars: JsCount`, breaking AC-012's unchanged-TypeScript-surface requirement and every downstream TypeScript consumer. Every converted position therefore carries an explicit TypeScript override, merged into the position's existing `#[napi(...)]` attribute where one is already present: `ts_type = "number"` on the four struct fields (JsToonValue::int_val, ::float_val, ::decimals_val, and JsToonOptions::total_count) and `ts_arg_type = "number"` on the two non-Option function/method parameters (truncate's max_chars, and JsAgentResponse::total_count's n). render_kv's total_count parameter is `Option<JsCount>`, not `JsCount`, and its override MUST be `ts_arg_type = "number | undefined | null"` -- a bare `"number"` override replaces the entire emitted argument type and silently drops the Option-driven nullable union that napi-rs would otherwise generate, which is a breaking TypeScript change verified by regenerating index.d.ts with each variant. These attributes are load-bearing, not cosmetic; each revised api_surface signature below shows the exact attribute placement.

CALL SITES CONVERTED (all line numbers re-derived from the current src/napi.rs at the time of writing):
1. JsToonValue.int_val: Option<i64> (src/napi.rs:53) becomes Option<JsInt>. NOTE: the i32-to-i64 widening was already performed by SPEC-NAPI-POINTFIX-001 (commit 2a8d38a); the widening is NOT this spec's deliverable. This spec's deliverable for int_val is adding range and integrality VALIDATION, which the widening did not add -- an intVal of 1.5 currently renders as 1 and an intVal beyond 2^53 currently loses precision silently.
2. JsToonValue.float_val: Option<f64> (src/napi.rs:56) becomes Option<JsFloat>. This input was omitted entirely from SPEC-ARCH-002 and is the same defect class: a raw f64 on the boundary with no NaN/Infinity check.
3. JsToonValue.decimals_val: Option<i32> (src/napi.rs:62) becomes Option<JsDecimals>, deleting the `.clamp(0, 20) as u8` at src/napi.rs:237.
4. JsToonOptions.total_count: Option<i32> (src/napi.rs:78) becomes Option<JsCount>, deleting the `.map(usize::try_from).and_then(Result::ok)` at src/napi.rs:136.
5. render_kv's total_count: Option<i32> parameter (src/napi.rs:248) becomes Option<JsCount>, deleting the `.map(|n| n.max(0) as usize)` at src/napi.rs:258.
6. truncate's max_chars: i32 parameter (src/napi.rs:219) becomes JsCount, deleting the `.max(0) as usize` at src/napi.rs:220. truncate's signature stays `-> String` (not napi::Result<String>): a FromNapiValue failure is thrown by the napi-derive-generated glue before the function body runs.
7. JsAgentResponse::total_count(n: i32) (src/napi.rs:516) becomes total_count(n: JsCount), deleting the `n.max(0) as usize` at src/napi.rs:518.

CAST-ALLOW ATTRIBUTES REMOVED: src/napi.rs currently carries exactly four `#[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation, clippy::cast_sign_loss)]` attributes -- at line 217 (truncate), line 247 (render_kv), line 325 (is_retryable_status), and line 515 (JsAgentResponse::total_count). Three of those four are in this spec's scope and are DELETED, not relocated: 217, 247, and 515. The one at line 325 (is_retryable_status) is resilience-domain and is left exactly as it is; the resilience spec removes it.

LINT ENFORCEMENT ADDED IN THIS SPEC (not deferred to the harness spec -- this is initial enforcement proving the fix is real, not future-regression prevention): src/napi.rs gains the module-level inner attribute `#![deny(clippy::as_conversions, clippy::cast_possible_truncation, clippy::cast_sign_loss, clippy::cast_possible_wrap, clippy::cast_precision_loss)]`. This is what makes deleting the three cast-allow attributes above meaningful rather than cosmetic: without the deny, a future author could silently reintroduce `as usize` at any of the three converted sites and `just check` would stay green.

EXISTING TESTS WITH AN EXPLICIT DISPOSITION: `truncate_clamps_negative_max_chars` in src/napi.rs mod tests (currently at src/napi.rs:875) -- DELETED and replaced by a Node test asserting rejection, because after the change a negative maxChars cannot be constructed in Rust at all (JsCount has no infallible constructor) and the Rust test is therefore unwritable, not merely wrong. `AC-008 truncates a non-integer intVal toward zero with no error` in packages/michi-node/__test__/index.test.mjs (currently at line 283) -- REWRITTEN to assert that intVal 1.5 throws.

EXISTING TEST CALL SITES THAT WILL FAIL TO COMPILE AND MUST BE MIGRATED: beyond the two dispositions above, ELEVEN further call sites in src/napi.rs mod tests construct the converted fields or parameters with bare numeric literals and will therefore fail to COMPILE (not merely change behavior) the moment the field types change, because the new types deliberately have no infallible constructor. All eleven are in scope for this spec and every one of them must be migrated. Verified sites, by current line number: src/napi.rs:745 (`int_val: Some(1)` in render_toon_basic), :746 (`total_count: Some(1)`, same JsToonOptions literal in render_toon_basic), :806 (`int_val: Some(1_755_000_000_000)` in render_toon_renders_int_beyond_i32_range), :871 (`truncate("hello".to_string(), 100, "full=true".to_string())` in truncate_basic), :884 (`int_val: Some(1)`), :927 (`int_val: Some(1)`), :928 (`int_val: Some(99)`), :939 (`int_val: Some(1)`), :941 (`int_val: Some(99)`), :1123 (`float_val: Some(3.14159)` in render_kv_napi_float_default_decimals), and :1133 (`float_val: Some(3.14159), decimals_val: Some(2)` in render_kv_napi_float_custom_decimals -- two constructions on one line, migrated together). Confirmed exhaustive by running `cargo check --features napi --lib --tests` against the fully-applied change; no further site errors.

SANCTIONED TEST CONSTRUCTION IDIOM: every one of those eleven sites is migrated to the fallible constructor plus an explanatory expect, e.g. `JsCount::try_from(100.0).expect("100 is a valid count")`, and the analogous `JsInt::try_from(1.0).expect(...)`, `JsFloat::try_from(3.14159).expect(...)`, `JsDecimals::try_from(2.0).expect(...)`. `.expect()` with a message is permitted here and only here: this project's CLAUDE.md non-negotiable reads 'No unwrap()/expect() in lib code (tests OK with message)', and all eleven sites are inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`. It is explicitly FORBIDDEN to work around these eleven sites instead of migrating them: no infallible constructor, no `From<usize>`/`From<i64>`/`From<f64>` impl, no `#[cfg(test)]`-gated `From` impl, no `new_unchecked`, and no test-only bypass of any kind may be added to src/napi/num.rs. Any such escape hatch would reopen the defect class from inside the crate and is a review-blocking violation of this spec.

TEST EXECUTION GATING: src/napi/num.rs's unit tests, and every test in src/napi.rs mod tests, are compiled only when the `napi` feature is enabled (src/lib.rs gates `pub mod napi` behind `#[cfg(feature = "napi")]`). `just test-rust` runs `cargo nextest run --workspace` with no features and therefore executes none of AC-001 through AC-011's Rust unit tests; they run under `just test-rust-all` (`--all-features`) and under `just test` (which invokes both). This is expected and not a gap -- it matches the project's existing convention for every other test in this module -- but is stated explicitly so an implementer running only `just test-rust` does not mistake a skip for a pass.

SIBLING SPEC FILES SUPERSEDED: .claude/specs/michi-root-napi.json AC-027, AC-030, AC-031, AC-041, AC-042, plus its api_surface entries for truncate/render_kv/JsAgentResponse::total_count. .claude/specs/napi-boundary-point-fixes.json AC-007, AC-008, and AC-011 (its AC-001 through AC-006, AC-009, and AC-010 -- the other eight criteria in that eleven-criterion file -- are NOT superseded and remain live). AC-008 of that file asserts intVal 1.5 renders as '1' and throws no error, which this spec's AC-004 inverts. AC-011 of that file requires the docs' Numeric boundary section to state that intVal carries silent precision loss beyond Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, which this spec's AC-004 turns into a rejection -- a direct contradiction inside the very paragraph this spec's AC-013 rewrites. AC-007 of that file requires 'no edit to any existing test body', which the twelve migrations above (the eleven compile-forced sites plus the deleted truncate_clamps_negative_max_chars) violate by construction. .claude/specs/structural-napi-numeric-boundary-narrow-inconsistent-i32-coercion-across-multiple-call-sites.json (SPEC-ARCH-002) is marked superseded-not-implemented: its purpose field is prefixed with "SUPERSEDED BY SPEC-ARCH-003 (rendering) and its resilience-domain sibling -- never implemented", and none of its 16 acceptance criteria are treated as live by any downstream planning or gating agent. The file is retained, not deleted, because its resilience-domain criteria remain source material for the sibling spec's drafter. Three of SPEC-ARCH-002's rendering-domain criteria describe verification that has no automatic successor once SPEC-ARCH-002 itself goes dead, and are explicitly absorbed into this spec rather than dropped: its AC-007 (positive cross-entry-point agreement for a large in-domain value) is folded into this spec's AC-008; its AC-015 (absence of residual open-coded coercion expressions, not just cast-allow attributes) is folded into this spec's AC-011; and its AC-003 (the module-level clippy deny-lint configuration itself) is folded into this spec's AC-010. SPEC-ARCH-002's AC-006 (Node-level beyond-2^53 rejection) and AC-016 (insta-snapshot zero-diff requirement) have direct counterparts already in this spec's AC-004/AC-009 and AC-013(d) respectively and need no separate absorption.

DOCS: the '### Numeric boundary' section of docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md (heading currently at line 162) is rewritten to the rejection-based contract for total_count, decimalsVal, maxChars, intVal, and floatVal, using the camelCase JS field spellings so AC-013(a)'s substring assertions are well-defined against the rewritten text.",
  "non_goals": [
    "The resilience-domain half of the same defect class (next_retry_delay, is_retryable_status) -- covered by a future sibling spec reusing JsRanged and JsFloat.",
    "Designing JsFinite, JsNonNegFinite, JsRetryCount, or JsHttpStatus -- resilience spec's job. This spec names its float type JsFloat (not JsFinite) so the resilience spec can reuse it directly.",
    "The boundary-enforcement harness -- a trybuild compile-fail case pinning the JsRanged::get_u8 width mismatch, the syn-based no-new-raw-primitive scanner over src/napi.rs, and that scanner's non-vacuity fixture test. Split out into a sibling 'NAPI boundary raw-primitive enforcement harness' spec, because none of it is required to eliminate the defect class (the newtypes alone make a fifth coercion policy unrepresentable; the harness only prevents a future regression) and it shares no code with the newtypes themselves. It also adds trybuild and syn as dev-dependencies with an accompanying cargo-deny licence pre-check, an entirely separate tooling blast radius. That sibling spec is implemented after this one lands, since its scanner needs the post-fix src/napi.rs as its baseline violation set. NOTE: this is distinct from the module-level clippy deny-lint (AC-010) and the plain-substring residual-coercion scan (AC-011), both of which ship in THIS spec because they prove the fix is real today, not because they guard against a future regression -- only the syn-based structural scanner (which understands #[napi(object)] fields vs. arbitrary code) is deferred.",
    "Point patches to individual sites -- would leave the class intact.",
    "Changing internal numeric representations of michi-core/michi-toon/michi-truncate -- the defect is in the boundary, not the core. Existing defensive NaN handling in crates/michi-toon/src/render.rs:185 and crates/michi-core/src/kv/mod.rs:89-98 stays -- this spec makes those paths unreachable from JS, not deleted.",
    "Introducing BigInt into the public TypeScript surface.",
    "Non-numeric boundary validation (MAX_ROWS/MAX_FIELDS/MAX_HINTS caps, ToonOptions::validate() surfacing, unrecognized-type-string fallthrough).",
    "Outbound numeric positions (parse_retry_after's -> Option<f64>, next_retry_delay's return type) -- no coercion hazard on the way out.",
    "Private struct fields that are not boundary inputs -- JsAgentResponse::hint_count/::recovery_count (src/napi.rs:466,468) are usize but never read from JS, and must not be flagged by the raw-primitive scanner when the sibling enforcement-harness spec lands.",
    "Applying the same discipline to a future WASM or CLI boundary."
  ],
  "api_surface": [
    {
      "name": "JsCount",
      "signature": "pub struct JsCount(usize);
impl JsCount { pub const fn get(self) -> usize; }
impl TryFrom<f64> for JsCount { type Error = String; }
impl napi::bindgen_prelude::TypeName for JsCount { /* value_type() -> napi::ValueType::Number */ }
impl napi::bindgen_prelude::ValidateNapiValue for JsCount { /* required by napi-derive argument codegen */ }
impl napi::bindgen_prelude::FromNapiValue for JsCount { /* reads via f64::from_napi_value, then TryFrom */ }
impl napi::bindgen_prelude::ToNapiValue for JsCount { /* writes the stored usize back as a JS double */ }",
      "description": "A JavaScript number accepted only when it is finite, has no fractional part, is >= 0, and is <= 9007199254740991 (Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER). Stores usize directly, so there is no coercion left at any call site. TryFrom<f64> returns Err(format!("expected a non-negative integer no greater than 9007199254740991, got {v}")) on any other input; FromNapiValue wraps that string in napi::Error::new(napi::Status::InvalidArg, msg). TypeName and ValidateNapiValue are not optional -- napi-derive emits a ValidateNapiValue call for every #[napi] function argument, so omitting either is a compile error at each converted call site. Used at four positions: JsToonOptions.total_count (Option<JsCount>), render_kv's total_count parameter (Option<JsCount>), truncate's max_chars parameter (JsCount), and JsAgentResponse::total_count's n parameter (JsCount). Deliberately has no infallible constructor -- there is no From<usize>, no new(), and no pub field -- so a negative or fractional count is not merely discouraged but unrepresentable in Rust. Rust tests construct it as JsCount::try_from(100.0).expect("100 is a valid count")."
    },
    {
      "name": "JsInt",
      "signature": "pub struct JsInt(i64);
impl JsInt { pub const fn get(self) -> i64; }
impl TryFrom<f64> for JsInt { type Error = String; }
impl napi::bindgen_prelude::TypeName for JsInt { /* value_type() -> napi::ValueType::Number */ }
impl napi::bindgen_prelude::ValidateNapiValue for JsInt
impl napi::bindgen_prelude::FromNapiValue for JsInt
impl napi::bindgen_prelude::ToNapiValue for JsInt",
      "description": "A JavaScript number accepted only when it is finite, has no fractional part, and lies within [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991] -- the range over which a JS number and an i64 agree exactly. Stores i64. TryFrom<f64> returns Err(format!("expected an integer in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991], got {v}")) otherwise. Used at JsToonValue.int_val (Option<JsInt>), which feeds both js_value_to_rust (michi_toon::Value::Int) and js_kv_value_to_rust (crate::kv::KvValue::Int). Closes two silent-corruption paths the SPEC-NAPI-POINTFIX-001 widening left open: a fractional intVal (1.5 currently renders as 1) and an intVal beyond 2^53 (currently loses precision without a diagnostic). Rust tests construct it as JsInt::try_from(1.0).expect("1 is a valid int")."
    },
    {
      "name": "JsRanged",
      "signature": "pub struct JsRanged<const MIN: i64, const MAX: i64>(i64);
impl<const MIN: i64, const MAX: i64> JsRanged<MIN, MAX> {
    const U8_FITS: () = assert!(MIN >= 0 && MAX <= u8::MAX as i64, "JsRanged bounds do not fit in u8");
    pub const fn get(self) -> i64;
    // NOT `const fn`: u8::try_from cannot be called inside a const fn on this
    // workspace's pinned rustc 1.96 (E0658 -- TryFrom is not yet a const trait).
    pub fn get_u8(self) -> u8 {
        let () = Self::U8_FITS;
        u8::try_from(self.0).unwrap_or(u8::MAX)
    }
}
impl<const MIN: i64, const MAX: i64> TryFrom<f64> for JsRanged<MIN, MAX> { type Error = String; }
impl<const MIN: i64, const MAX: i64> napi::bindgen_prelude::TypeName for JsRanged<MIN, MAX> { /* value_type() -> napi::ValueType::Number */ }
impl<const MIN: i64, const MAX: i64> napi::bindgen_prelude::ValidateNapiValue for JsRanged<MIN, MAX>
impl<const MIN: i64, const MAX: i64> napi::bindgen_prelude::FromNapiValue for JsRanged<MIN, MAX>
impl<const MIN: i64, const MAX: i64> napi::bindgen_prelude::ToNapiValue for JsRanged<MIN, MAX>",

Base directory for this skill: /Users/gabe/.claude/plugins/cache/orin-dx-agent-plugins/lambda/1.2.0/skills/lambda

# Lambda — Implementation Skill

<sub_skills>

| Sub-skill | What it does |
| :--- | :--- |
| `lambda/implement` | Executes a single task from a plan@1 via the full TDD cycle: failing test → minimal code → commit. |
| `lambda/generate-tests` | Writes a complete test suite for a spec or module without changing implementation code. |
| `lambda/explain` | Reads a module or function and produces a plain-language explanation of what it does and why. |
| `lambda/refactor` | Restructures code for clarity or performance without changing observable behavior; tests must stay green throughout. |

</sub_skills>

---

<io>

**Consumes**: `plan@1` (preferred) or `spec@1` directly if no plan exists.

**Produces**: committed code, and per-task `criteria_evidence` (exact test and implementation file/line for each criterion proven). No lambda agent assembles a `changeset@1` itself — that schema is produced by `delta-changeset-analyzer` when shipping. The caller aggregates each task's `criteria_evidence` across the run and hands the collection to `delta-changeset-analyzer` alongside the diff, so delta uses lambda's exact evidence instead of reconstructing approximate locations from the diff.

</io>

---

<tdd_cycle>

For every implementation task:

1. Write the failing test exactly as specified.
2. Run the test — confirm it fails with the expected error (red phase required; a test that passes before implementation is broken).
3. Write the minimal implementation to make it pass — no more.
4. Run the test — confirm it passes (green).
5. Commit with the conventional commit message specified in the task.

</tdd_cycle>

---

<mutation_gate>

After each implementation task commits, `lambda-mutator` runs mutation testing scoped to the files changed in that task. It detects language from the workspace root (Cargo.toml → `cargo-mutants`; package.json → Stryker) and analyzes every mutant the test suite failed to catch.

For each surviving mutant, `lambda-mutator` designs a precision test that would kill it and returns those tests to `lambda-implementer` as additional failing tests. The implementer writes them and makes them green before any further tasks proceed.

When the mutation tool is unavailable, `lambda-mutator` reports `tool_unavailable` and `lambda-exit-gate` records the gap rather than blocking.

</mutation_gate>

---

<exit_gate>

After all tasks are complete and `lambda-mutator` has run, `lambda-exit-gate` runs the axiom protocol against the spec independently. It reads the spec from `spec_file_path` on disk — not from spec content forwarded through conversation context. It reads the current code state from scratch, assumes the implementation is incomplete, and confirms that mutation testing ran (or was noted as unavailable). It returns a `verdict@1`. A spec without `spec_file_path` set is a hard block.

The caller passes the aggregated per-task `criteria_evidence` to `lambda-exit-gate` alongside the manifest. The gate uses each entry as a pointer to check — reading exactly the named file and line — rather than searching the codebase cold for every criterion. This makes verification faster without making it less adversarial: the gate still reads the actual location itself and confirms the criterion holds; it does not accept the pointer's existence as proof.

</exit_gate>

---

<subagent_dispatch_matrix>

| Agent | Role | Tier | When to delegate |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`lambda-recon`** | Workspace manifest & baseline | haiku / low | Before any code is written — detect language, test runner, inventory plan files, confirm baseline passes. |
| **`lambda-implementer`** | TDD execution | sonnet / medium | One task at a time from the plan@1 — full red/green/commit cycle. Re-invoked when lambda-mutator returns precision tests. |
| **`lambda-mutator`** | Mutation testing gate | sonnet / medium | After each implementer commit — verify the test suite would catch real faults; return precision tests for any survivors. |
| **`lambda-reviewer`** | Pre-gate review | sonnet / medium | After mutation gate passes — neutral review of scope, non-negotiables, sibling gaps, test quality. |
| **`lambda-exit-gate`** | Adversarial exit verification | opus / high | After all tasks and mutation gate complete — independent axiom check against spec; produces verdict@1. |

</subagent_dispatch_matrix>

---

<context_management>

Lambda executes tasks sequentially. Each `lambda-implementer` invocation handles exactly one task. The orchestrating caller is responsible for keeping context lean across the sequence.

**Caller MUST pass per-invocation:**
- The current task object only (not the full `plan@1`).
- The workspace manifest from `lambda-recon` (file list + baseline status).
- `spec_file_path` from the plan@1 (propagated there by vector-planner from the spec@1) — pass it to lambda-recon so it flows through the workspace manifest to all downstream agents.
- Any `precision_tests` from `lambda-mutator` for the current task.

**Caller MUST NOT pass:**
- The full `plan@1` on every invocation — a 40-task plan passed 40 times consumes 320K–600K tokens on plan context alone.
- The full `spec@1` content on every invocation — pass `spec_file_path` instead; agents read from disk. Context is lossy under compression; the file is not.
- Prior task results — the commit SHA is sufficient to verify what happened.

**Progress tracking:** The caller tracks completed task IDs, their commit SHAs, and their `criteria_evidence` entries externally (in a progress note or equivalent). On re-entry after interruption, pass the remaining tasks, not the full list. The accumulated `criteria_evidence` across all completed tasks is what gets passed to `lambda-exit-gate` and later to `delta-changeset-analyzer` — do not discard it once a task completes.

**When `lambda-implementer` emits `needs_context`:** the caller resolves the missing information (file path, baseline commit) before re-invoking — do not retry with the same inputs.

**When `lambda-implementer` emits `spec_contradiction`:** the caller halts remaining task execution — already-completed tasks are not rolled back, but no further task proceeds against a spec known to be wrong. Route the contradiction (spec_file_path, criterion_id, spec_claim, observed_behavior) to canon/correct. Once the corrected spec passes canon-exit-gate and is written back to the same spec_file_path, route the corrected spec@1 to vector-planner in amend mode, then through vector-challenger — an amended plan is not exempt from adversarial review, especially for newly added tasks — before resuming lambda from the remaining tasks. The caller tracks correction attempts per criterion_id: if the same criterion_id triggers spec_contradiction a second time after already being corrected, escalate to a human rather than routing to canon/correct again.

</context_management>

mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn js_count_accepts_valid_domain() {
        for (v, expected) in
            [(0.0, 0usize), (1.0, 1), (42.0, 42), (1e6, 1_000_000), (9_007_199_254_740_991.0, 9_007_199_254_740_991)]
        {
            assert_eq!(JsCount::try_from(v).map(JsCount::get), Ok(expected), "input {v}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_count_rejects_out_of_domain() {
        for v in [-1.0, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5, f64::NAN, f64::INFINITY, f64::NEG_INFINITY, 9_007_199_254_740_992.0] {
            let err = JsCount::try_from(v).expect_err("out-of-domain value must be rejected");
            assert_eq!(err, format!("expected a non-negative integer no greater than 9007199254740991, got {v}"));
        }
    }

    fn js_int_accepts_safe_integers() {
        for (v, expected) in [
            (0.0, 0i64),
            (-1.0, -1),
            (1.0, 1),
            (-9_007_199_254_740_991.0, -9_007_199_254_740_991),
            (9_007_199_254_740_991.0, 9_007_199_254_740_991),
            (-1_755_000_000_000.0, -1_755_000_000_000),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(JsInt::try_from(v).map(JsInt::get), Ok(expected), "input {v}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_int_rejects_fractional_and_unsafe() {
        for v in
            [1.5, -1.5, f64::NAN, f64::INFINITY, f64::NEG_INFINITY, 9_007_199_254_740_992.0, -9_007_199_254_740_992.0]
        {
            let err = JsInt::try_from(v).expect_err("out-of-domain value must be rejected");
            assert_eq!(err, format!("expected an integer in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991], got {v}"));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_count_type_name_is_js_count() {
        assert_eq!(JsCount::type_name(), "JsCount");
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_int_type_name_is_js_int() {
        assert_eq!(JsInt::type_name(), "JsInt");
    }

        }
    }

    #[test]

        for v in [0.0, -0.0, 1.5, -1.5, f64::MAX, f64::MIN_POSITIVE] {

            let err = JsFloat::try_from(v).expect_err("non-finite value must be rejected");
            assert_eq!(err, format!("expected a finite number, got {v}"));
        }
    }

/// The shared kernel type for every bounded-integer position on the NAPI
/// boundary, in either domain. Accepts a JS number only when it is finite,
/// has no fractional part, and satisfies `MIN <= v <= MAX`. Generic and
/// reusable — not specialized to any single domain's bounds.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct JsRanged<const MIN: i64, const MAX: i64>(i64);

impl<const MIN: i64, const MAX: i64> JsRanged<MIN, MAX> {
    const U8_FITS: () = assert!(MIN >= 0 && MAX <= u8::MAX as i64, "JsRanged bounds do not fit in u8");

    /// Returns the validated integer.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn get(self) -> i64 {
        self.0
    }

    /// Returns the validated integer narrowed to `u8`. Only valid when
    /// `MIN >= 0 && MAX <= u8::MAX`; instantiating this function with
    /// bounds that don't fit `u8` is a compile error (`E0080`) via
    /// `U8_FITS`.
    // NOT `const fn`: `u8::try_from` cannot be called inside a const fn on
    // this workspace's pinned rustc 1.96 (E0658 — `TryFrom` is not yet a
    // const trait).
    pub fn get_u8(self) -> u8 {
        let () = Self::U8_FITS;
        u8::try_from(self.0).unwrap_or(u8::MAX)
    }
}

    type Error = String;

    fn try_from(v: f64) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
        if v.is_finite() && v.fract() == 0.0 && v >= MIN as f64 && v <= MAX as f64 {
            Ok(Self(v as i64))
        } else {
            Err(format!("expected an integer in [{MIN}, {MAX}], got {v}"))
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn js_count_accepts_valid_domain() {
        for (v, expected) in
            [(0.0, 0usize), (1.0, 1), (42.0, 42), (1e6, 1_000_000), (9_007_199_254_740_991.0, 9_007_199_254_740_991)]
        {
            assert_eq!(JsCount::try_from(v).map(JsCount::get), Ok(expected), "input {v}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_count_rejects_out_of_domain() {
        for v in [-1.0, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5, f64::NAN, f64::INFINITY, f64::NEG_INFINITY, 9_007_199_254_740_992.0] {
            let err = JsCount::try_from(v).expect_err("out-of-domain value must be rejected");
            assert_eq!(err, format!("expected a non-negative integer no greater than 9007199254740991, got {v}"));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_int_accepts_safe_integers() {
        for (v, expected) in [
            (0.0, 0i64),
            (-1.0, -1),
            (1.0, 1),
            (-9_007_199_254_740_991.0, -9_007_199_254_740_991),
            (9_007_199_254_740_991.0, 9_007_199_254_740_991),
            (-1_755_000_000_000.0, -1_755_000_000_000),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(JsInt::try_from(v).map(JsInt::get), Ok(expected), "input {v}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_int_rejects_fractional_and_unsafe() {
        for v in
            [1.5, -1.5, f64::NAN, f64::INFINITY, f64::NEG_INFINITY, 9_007_199_254_740_992.0, -9_007_199_254_740_992.0]
        {
            let err = JsInt::try_from(v).expect_err("out-of-domain value must be rejected");
            assert_eq!(err, format!("expected an integer in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991], got {v}"));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_count_type_name_is_js_count() {
        assert_eq!(JsCount::type_name(), "JsCount");
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_int_type_name_is_js_int() {
        assert_eq!(JsInt::type_name(), "JsInt");
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_decimals_accepts_zero_through_twenty() {
        for (v, expected) in [(0.0, 0u8), (6.0, 6), (20.0, 20)] {
            let d = JsDecimals::try_from(v).expect("in-domain decimals value");
            assert_eq!(d.get_u8(), expected, "input {v}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_decimals_rejects_out_of_range() {
        for v in [-1.0, 21.0, 6.5, f64::NAN, f64::INFINITY] {
            let err = JsDecimals::try_from(v).expect_err("out-of-range decimals value must be rejected");
            assert_eq!(err, format!("expected an integer in [0, 20], got {v}"));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_float_accepts_finite_rejects_nan_and_infinity() {
        for v in [0.0, -0.0, 1.5, -1.5, f64::MAX, f64::MIN_POSITIVE] {
            let f = JsFloat::try_from(v).expect("finite value must be accepted");
            assert_eq!(f.get().to_bits(), v.to_bits(), "input {v}");
        }
        for v in [f64::NAN, f64::INFINITY, f64::NEG_INFINITY] {
            let err = JsFloat::try_from(v).expect_err("non-finite value must be rejected");
            assert_eq!(err, format!("expected a finite number, got {v}"));
        }
    }

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn js_count_accepts_valid_domain() {
        for (v, expected) in
            [(0.0, 0usize), (1.0, 1), (42.0, 42), (1e6, 1_000_000), (9_007_199_254_740_991.0, 9_007_199_254_740_991)]
        {
            assert_eq!(JsCount::try_from(v).map(JsCount::get), Ok(expected), "input {v}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_count_rejects_out_of_domain() {
        for v in [-1.0, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5, f64::NAN, f64::INFINITY, f64::NEG_INFINITY, 9_007_199_254_740_992.0] {
            let err = JsCount::try_from(v).expect_err("out-of-domain value must be rejected");
            assert_eq!(err, format!("expected a non-negative integer no greater than 9007199254740991, got {v}"));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_int_accepts_safe_integers() {
        for (v, expected) in [
            (0.0, 0i64),
            (-1.0, -1),
            (1.0, 1),
            (-9_007_199_254_740_991.0, -9_007_199_254_740_991),
            (9_007_199_254_740_991.0, 9_007_199_254_740_991),
            (-1_755_000_000_000.0, -1_755_000_000_000),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(JsInt::try_from(v).map(JsInt::get), Ok(expected), "input {v}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_int_rejects_fractional_and_unsafe() {
        for v in
            [1.5, -1.5, f64::NAN, f64::INFINITY, f64::NEG_INFINITY, 9_007_199_254_740_992.0, -9_007_199_254_740_992.0]
        {
            let err = JsInt::try_from(v).expect_err("out-of-domain value must be rejected");
            assert_eq!(err, format!("expected an integer in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991], got {v}"));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_count_type_name_is_js_count() {
        assert_eq!(JsCount::type_name(), "JsCount");
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_int_type_name_is_js_int() {
        assert_eq!(JsInt::type_name(), "JsInt");
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_decimals_accepts_zero_through_twenty() {
        for (v, expected) in [(0.0, 0u8), (6.0, 6), (20.0, 20)] {
            let d = JsDecimals::try_from(v).expect("in-domain decimals value");
            assert_eq!(d.get_u8(), expected, "input {v}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_decimals_rejects_out_of_range() {
        for v in [-1.0, 21.0, 6.5, f64::NAN, f64::INFINITY] {
            let err = JsDecimals::try_from(v).expect_err("out-of-range decimals value must be rejected");
            assert_eq!(err, format!("expected an integer in [0, 20], got {v}"));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn js_float_accepts_finite_rejects_nan_and_infinity() {
        for v in [0.0, -0.0, 1.5, -1.5, f64::MAX, f64::MIN_POSITIVE] {
            let f = JsFloat::try_from(v).expect("finite value must be accepted");
            assert_eq!(f.get().to_bits(), v.to_bits(), "input {v}");
        }
        for v in [f64::NAN, f64::INFINITY, f64::NEG_INFINITY] {
            let err = JsFloat::try_from(v).expect_err("non-finite value must be rejected");
            assert_eq!(err, format!("expected a finite number, got {v}"));
        }
    }

  +## NAPI Boundary Contract
  +
  +The NAPI boundary (`src/napi.rs`) has a specific constructor discipline that differs from pure-Rust callers:
  +
  +**NAPI functions always use normalizing constructors (`new()`), never strict ones (`try_new()`).**
  +
  +- `RetryConfig::new()` normalizes out-of-range inputs silently (clamps `jitter_factor`, floors `max_delay`, etc.). `napi.rs:274` calls it this way; making it fallible there would require either `unwrap()`/`expect()` (banned) or a silent fallback to `Default` (defeats validation).
  +- Pure-Rust callers and tests may use `try_new()` / `validate()` for explicit error signals.
  +- JS-facing functions report errors via `napi::Error`, not `Result` propagation — validation that can't be normalized (truly invalid JS input) becomes a JS exception at the boundary, not a Rust panic.
  +
  +This asymmetry is intentional. The NAPI layer operates in a "be maximally resilient to JS input, fail loudly only for truly unrecoverable cases" mode; the Rust library layer operates in a "signal problems explicitly through types" mode.
  +
  +**Error output path:** When you hold a `DomainError`, call `domain_error.to_call_tool_result()` directly.
